text:
ana: Heads-up — after the autotune landing this morning I'm seeing a p50 regression on long-context prefill workloads (~12% higher). Posted traces + perf counters below.

sam: ugh. which autotune change? the kernel muxer rewrite?

jordan: yes, we changed the architecture-aware pick to bias toward the fused matmul kernel for seqlen > 2048 to save tokens on decode paths. prefill path was supposed to still prefer the lightweight prefiller kernel but the gating looks like it flipped.

kevin: I pulled a perf sample:
```
prefill: chosen_kernel=fused_matmul_v2  (previous: prefill_shallow)
seq_len=3072 tokens
GPU_util=92% -> spiky memcpy stall at KV write
KV_cache_evictions++  at 1.8x
latency_p50=238ms -> 268ms
```

ana: interesting — KV cache thrashing due to larger kernel's bigger temp buffers?

jordan: exactly. fused_matmul_v2 uses a different workspace layout and forces an extra KV prefetch in the prefill code path that increases peak memory working set. That causes cross-slab eviction and slower memcpy. On microbench we didn't see it because microbench small batch sizes. Production batches are larger and it hits eviction threshold.

sam: any quick mitigations we can push? revert gating? override kernel pick for prefill only?

kevin: I put a canary patch that forces prefill to use prefill_shallow when seqlen >= 1024 and batch_size >= 8. Canary run shows p50 back to 240ms and KV_evictions down. Canary token throughput dropped ~1.5% but latency recovers.

canary-bot: Canary deployed to canary-io-3 at 1939012365 — 30m window. Metrics: p50 latency -10%, KV evictions -55% vs prod baseline.

ana: sounds reasonable to me as an immediate fix. Need a proper autotune update to consider working set impact (workspace memory) not just FLOPS. Current cost function only looked at kernel cycles.

jordan: agreed. Plan: revert muxer gating for prefill, ship a microbench that uses batched long-context prefill workloads to reproduce eviction, and extend autotune feature vector with 'workspace_peak_bytes' and 'kv_prefetch_flag'. I can PR today.

sam: add an integration test: spawn a 4x batch longctx prefill session and assert KV_evictions==0 or below threshold. That will catch this.

kevin: I'll keep the canary live until PR lands + 1 canary run. Also we should backfill metrics for last 48h to see if any customer traffic got affected.

ana: one more note — we might want a fallback policy: if chosen kernel increases working_set by >20% relative to alternative, prefer the lower-memory kernel unless throughput win > 12%. That should avoid noisy regressions.

jordan: good heuristic. I'll add it to the autotune objective and run an offline simulation against replayed traces.

sam: thanks all — please drop short status updates in this thread. If anyone needs me I can help with the canary dashboards. :thumbsup:
